idiom_name: domain-vocabulary naming + precise signatures + one operation per legal action
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: derive every name on the interface from the domain vocabulary and state effect and purpose, never mechanism; make parameters and results precise enough that the signature alone rules out the wrong call; give each legal action its own named operation instead of a parameterised 'do it' entry point; and document only what the types cannot express (pre/postconditions, failure, cost). Write the first client call - or its test - before the operation exists, so the name is designed from the caller's side; that is also the cheapest moment to rename.
code_sketch:
interface Order            # names the domain concept
    forCart(cart, buyer)   # named constructor, not Order(...)
    addLine(sku, qty)      # command: verb phrase, one legal action
    total() -> Money       # query: noun phrase, no side effects
    isCancellable() -> bool
# no operation takes a mode/flag that selects between the operations above
pitfalls: Parameterised 'action' methods (`process(action, payload)`) push the implementation back onto the caller - split them into one named operation per legal action.
Names that describe the algorithm survive refactoring only by accident: when the mechanism changes they become wrong, and callers who trusted them break.
Renaming a published interface is a breaking change, so plan deprecation (alias plus migration note) rather than renaming silently.
